decision:
I confirm the overturn from the audit's OPEN to NARROWED. The verifiers did not share an error on the grade. I read arXiv:1105.4714v1, pp. 1-12, myself through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries. The Nature version was not read.

What the source says:
- The claim, from the abstract (p. 2): "Using a superconducting circuit, we have observed the DCE for the first time ... modulating the inductance of a SQUID at high frequencies (~11 GHz) ... we observe two-mode squeezing of the emitted radiation."
- The conclusion (p. 11): "we believe these results represent the first experimental observation of the dynamical Casimir effect."
- What was measured: the photon flux n_out (Eq. 2), broadband output power, and two-mode squeezing.
- Energy density: the paper neither measures nor claims any energy density. The only related passage is the static Casimir radiation pressure (p. 2).

The audit's four hypotheses, each stated in the paper:
- H1, the observable: photon generation.
- H2, the boundary: an effective circuit boundary. Its velocity is the rate of change of the electrical length, with v/c ~ 0.05 at 10% inductance modulation (p. 3) and c0 ~ 0.4c (p. 4).
- H3, thermal input ruled out: the sample is at 50 mK, giving n = 0.008 at 5 GHz. I recomputed 0.0083. An 8.4-12 GHz bandpass filter sits on the drive line, and the broadband output excludes a single-mode parametric amplifier.
- H4, the quantum signature: <I+I-> = -<Q+Q->, cross-correlations about 100 times the amplifier's own, single-mode fields unsqueezed, and Psi -> e^{-2i theta} Psi.

The grade, use by use:
- Use 1, "DCE is real and observed" (warpfolder.py:155, and the words "DYNAMICAL CASIMIR MEASURED" at achievable.py:33), STANDS as the authors' claim.
- Use 2 is the row's placement under "THE CENSUS OF KNOWN NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY -- Everything real" (achievable.py:27-28, with "stands item by item" at :24-25), repeated at research/README.md:2828/2835 and paper/CLAIMS.md:668-669. Placed there, the row reads as a measured negative-energy-density source. It holds only on a smaller class: a measured photon-generation and two-mode-squeezing effect. That is NARROWED.
- It is not WRONG. No site states outright that Wilson measured a negative density, and DCE is real, so nothing refutes the row. This is a placement over-reach by the tree, not an error by Wilson et al. achievable.py's NO verdict does not rest on this row.

The re-derivation:
- I copied it to adjudicate/run/w.py and ran it: ALL PASS, exit 0, every figure identical to the audit's. The script is byte-identical to the copy in docket67-raw.
- It bears only on the warpfolder NOT-ADJUDICATED hedge. It supports that hedge under a named hypothesis: the motion begins and ends inertial. Verifier 2's vacuity guard shows that hypothesis is load-bearing.
corrections_to_record: The audit's OPEN, its NAMED-NOT-READ status and every 'value_then: not read' are superseded. arXiv:1105.4714v1 was read in full this pass.
The drive frequency is now READ: '~11 GHz' in the abstract, an 8-12 GHz band, and 8.70 and 11.30 GHz in Figs 2-3. The audit's untraced ~11 GHz was correct.

Effective velocity, read at source: 'a few percent of the speed of light', and 'v/c ~ 0.05 for a 10% modulation of the SQUID inductance' (p. 3). The '10%' is the inductance modulation, not the velocity.

Internal discrepancy in the source, recorded and not adjudicated. With sigma2 ~ v_e/2c0, v/c ~ 0.05 and c0 ~ 0.4c, sigma2 comes to ~0.06. The paper instead says 'about 2%', which implies v_e/c0 ~ 0.04. It then measures sigma2 ~ 0.04 and calls this 'consistent'. Fig 3c's squeezing axis, as extracted, spans 0-2.0%. The text does not settle whether 0.05 is taken against c or c0.

Named hypothesis: the measured power ('a few Kelvin') exceeds the ideal-line prediction ('a few mK'). The paper reconciles the two with a Q^2 enhancement from parasitic resonances at Q ~ 30-50, giving a factor of 1000-2000. The absolute rate rests on that model inference; the qualitative observation does not.
Named limitation: the thermal occupation is inferred from the fridge temperature (50 mK), not from a measured mode temperature.
Path correction: the audit's 'README.md:2835' is research/README.md:2835, outside research/warp-drive/. It is a table under the heading '### The census of real negative energy density' at line 2828.
The audit cited paper/CLAIMS.md:5495-5496 for the 'squeezed vacuum ... negative energy density' text. That text now sits at line 5496.
The re-derivation's 'negative on 50% of the grid' counts tail points where the flux is negligible. Among points with |F| > 1e-8 the negative fraction is 0.49. Not materially wrong.
The Fulling-Davies flux formula used in the re-derivation remains recalled, not read. Wilson cites it as ref 17 without stating it.
The later literature (Lahteenmaki 2013 PNAS, 1405.3720, 1411.2948, 2504.11361) remains NAMED-NOT-READ. One discover_papers search, run by a verifier, found no dispute, which does not rule one out.

tree_sites.finding: 'DYNAMICAL CASIMIR MEASURED (Wilson 2011, superconducting circuit)' is true of the effect. Placed under the census of negative energy density, it goes beyond the source: no energy density was measured. The line number is current.
The header 'THE CENSUS OF KNOWN NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY / Everything real, and what bounds it' attaches the negative-density reading to the Wilson row.
'The census of real negative-energy sources below stands item by item.' For the DCE item it stands only as a measured photon effect.
'DCE is real and observed; that it gives a usable STATIC negative density ... is the unestablished step.' This STANDS against the source; the hedge is supported.
The NOT_ADJUDICATED tuple holding the shear-gap DCE claim is consistent with the source and with the re-derivation.
'The census of real negative energy density -- ... dynamical Casimir (measured, Wilson 2011)'. The same placement over-reach.

tree_sites.site: research/README.md:2835 (outside warp-drive; the audit cited it as README.md:2835)
tree_sites.finding: A table under '### The census of real negative energy density' (line 2828) reads 'dynamical Casimir | measured -- Wilson 2011'. The same placement over-reach.

DCE_DRIVEN_AT_HZ = 1e9, against Wilson's read 8-12 GHz, about one decade low. frequency.py sources its DCE to arXiv:2504.11361, not to Wilson. The gap is 32.7-32.9 decades at the read drive frequencies against 33.77 at 1 GHz, and the verdict does not move. Not an owner site.

'squeezed vacuum, which carries regions of NEGATIVE energy density' cites arXiv:2504.11361, not Wilson, and is not adjudicated here. Read together with the Wilson citations elsewhere, it produces the over-reach.
The audit cited lines 5495-5496. The squeezed-vacuum negative-energy text is now at 5496.
